newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close firm, US dollar stocks up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close firm, US dollar stocks up.

text.p: Singapore shares close firmer on Wednesday with US dollar denominated stocks leading the gains.
"There seems to be renewed interest in US dollar stocks, probably a spill over effect from the rise in Jardine group shares," a dealer with a Singapore brokerage said.
Jardine units, led by Hongkong Land, saw active trading on continued speculation that a takeover was on the cards for Hongkong Land.
After hitting an intraday high of US$3.56, the stock closed 28 cents up at US$3.40 with 49 million shares traded.
Other gainers included CM Telecom, which gained four cents to US$0.38, and Huan Hsin, which six cents to US$0.78 in active trade.
The Straits Times Industrial Index ended at 1,958.62 up 6.91 points. Total volume was 262.5 million units with 272 gainers against 108 losers.
Dealers said electronic stocks rose after recent price falls. Among the top gainers was Creative Technology which rose S$1.90 to S$32.90.
Sound-maker Aztech Systems gained half a cent to S$0.63 on expectations of better results.
The local and foreign tranches of DBS Bank also gained leading up to the release of its interim results.
Its half-year profits rose 13 percent to S$358.29 million.
DBS Bank rose five cents to S$8.80, while its foreign tranche rose 50 cents to S$18.80.
